subject.title: System prompt should prefer Skill tool over read when available

question: Should OpenClaw support a plugin-provided Skill loader in the native Skills prompt by raw tool name, by an explicit trusted capability/contract, or defer it until broader skill-contract work is settled?
rationale: Choosing how plugin tool output becomes higher-authority skill-loading context changes prompt precedence and the native plugin trust boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Require Explicit Skill-Loader Capability
options.body: Add a named trusted capability or manifest/SDK contract before changing prompt wording, so only intentionally declared loader tools receive the stronger loading instruction.

options.title: Use Normalized Tool Name Detection
options.body: Treat any available tool named Skill as the loader and update the prompt now, accepting the collision and trust-boundary risk for a smaller change.

options.title: Defer To Broader Skill Contract Work
options.body: Keep the read-based prompt until native/Codex parity, slash invocation, and instruction-isolation semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Skill-Loader Capability
recommendation.body: Add a named trusted capability or manifest/SDK contract before changing prompt wording, so only intentionally declared loader tools receive the stronger loading instruction.
